entry.title: There's a global pandemic treaty that's signed -- and in 'limbo.' What's the holdup?
entry.summary: The treaty aims to help the countries of the world prepare for — and defeat — any future pandemic. Why hasn't it gone into effect?

entry.title: Mom! Mom! MOM! 3 ways to stay calm in stressful parenting moments
entry.summary: Parenthood can be overwhelming. A therapist and mom of three shares techniques to help calibrate your emotions — so you can show up better for yourself and your family.

entry.title: Congress passed $100 million for teen pregnancy prevention. Most of it is untouched
entry.summary: With days left to go in the 2026 fiscal year, lawmakers push the health department to spend the money Congress allocated to prevent teen pregnancy. An NPR exclusive.

entry.title: President Trump's FDA commissioner nom, Dr. Heidi Overton, faces Senators' questions
entry.summary: Dr. Heidi Overton has been nominated to be the new FDA commissioner. The Senate HELP committee pressed her on vaccines, mifepristone, food safety and whether she can tell the president he's wrong.

entry.title: How to limit rat numbers? Train humans
entry.summary: No matter how much poison you put out, rats continue to thrive. So D.C.'s Rat Rangers are trying education (of people, not the rats). They take residents into back alleys to illuminate the problem.

entry.title: RFK Jr.'s ethics filing reveals book deals worth millions of dollars
entry.summary: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s annual financial disclosure reveals he has received two lucrative book advances and free flights from a friend while in office.

entry.title: Needy couples got cash and a spending plan. Results were good -- and bad
entry.summary: In Liberia, joint financial planning boosted cash aid's benefits. It also had an unexpected consequence for some families.

entry.title: These 6 charts show how NIH research funding has been reshaped under Trump
entry.summary: Stories of science funding being cut, labs shutting down and scientists losing jobs have flooded the media under Trump's administration. These six graphics show how those changes have affected U.S. biomedical research.

entry.title: New research suggests human actions could be driving increase in disease outbreaks
entry.summary: Infectious disease outbreaks are on the rise worldwide. A new analysis finds human actions, from deforestation to climate change, are partly responsible.

entry.title: Is Nepal's flood a harbinger of what's to come in the Himalayas?
entry.summary: Building dams and hydropower plants in the Himalayas holds great promise for providing electricity. In the wake of the Nepal disaster, experts are asking about the risks of such construction.
